descripcion: At C1, comparison moves past simple comparatives into weighted, qualified contrast: acknowledging that two things are similar in one respect and different in another, without collapsing the nuance into a flat this is better than that.

filas: They're similar in scope, though not in ambition.
On balance, I'd lean towards the first, but only just.
Both share the same underlying assumption.
Where they really diverge is in execution.

ejemplos.texto: They're similar in scope, though not in ambition.
On balance, I'd lean towards the first option, but only just.
Where they really diverge is in how each handles failure.

notas: Naming shared ground before the contrast makes the comparison feel fair rather than one-sided.
But only just is a useful qualifier that keeps a preference from sounding absolute.
Where they really diverge is in… isolates the single dimension that matters most, instead of listing every difference.

es.en: Spanish has the pieces for a graded comparison («en conjunto» – on balance; «por poco» – only just), so the structure transfers. The compact English form on balance…, but only just is worth learning as one unit.
es.es: El español tiene los elementos para una comparación graduada («en conjunto» – «on balance»; «por poco» – «only just»), por lo que la estructura se transfiere. La forma inglesa compacta «on balance…, but only just» conviene aprenderla como una unidad.

de.en: German has close equivalents: «unterm Strich» (on balance) and «knapp» (only just: «knapp besser» – only just better). Graded comparison therefore transfers directly.
de.de: Das Deutsche hat nahe Entsprechungen: «unterm Strich» für «on balance» und «knapp» für «only just» («knapp besser» – «only just better»). Abgestufte Vergleiche lassen sich daher direkt übertragen.

it.en: Italian has close equivalents: «tutto sommato» (on balance) and «di poco» (only just). Graded comparison therefore transfers directly.
it.it: L'italiano ha equivalenti vicini: «tutto sommato» («on balance») e «di poco» («only just»). La comparazione graduata si trasferisce quindi direttamente.

fr.en: French has close equivalents: «tout bien considéré» (on balance) and «de justesse» (only just). Graded comparison therefore transfers directly.
fr.fr: Le français a des équivalents proches : «tout bien considéré» («on balance») et «de justesse» («only just»). La comparaison graduée se transfère donc directement.

pt.en: Portuguese has close equivalents: «feitas as contas» (on balance) and «por pouco» (only just). Graded comparison therefore transfers directly.
pt.pt: O português tem equivalentes próximos: «feitas as contas» («on balance») e «por pouco» («only just»). A comparação graduada se transfere diretamente.

errores: Comparing without naming any shared ground first, which makes the contrast feel one-sided.
Stating a preference as absolute when the actual difference is marginal.
Listing every difference instead of isolating the one dimension that matters most.

es: «*A diferencia de*» rendered as *At difference of* instead of *Unlike*.
de: «*Im Gegensatz zu*» rendered as *In opposite to* instead of *In contrast to*.
it: «*A differenza di*» rendered as *At difference of* instead of *Unlike*.
fr: «*À la différence de*» rendered as *At the difference of* instead of *Unlike*.
pt: «*Ao contrário de*» rendered as *At the contrary of* instead of *Unlike* or *Contrary to*.

mision.consigna: Compare the family culture you grew up in with one you've seen up close in another country or household.
requisitos: one *similar in X, though not in Y*
use *a close-knit family*, *shared values* and *to grow apart*

microtareas.texto: List three things two families you know have in common and three where they differ.
Write two sentences with *It's less a question of X and more one of Y* about *being there for someone*.
Record 90 seconds: is it easier to *fall out* with family or with friends? Weigh, don't declare.

autochequeo: Is shared ground named before the contrast?
Is any stated preference appropriately qualified rather than absolute?
Is the comparison focused on the one dimension that matters most?
Would a listener sense fairness or one-sidedness in the comparison?
Have I avoided listing every possible difference instead of picking the key one?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on how the comparison is structured: shared ground, qualified preference, key dimension of difference. Say whether the comparison feels fair or one-sided, and flag any preference stated as absolute when it isn't. Do not rewrite the text.
